cases.note: Thirty seconds at the default factor of two.
A site that will tolerate half again as long.
A factor under one would stop a skill before its own estimate, which is not an overrun factor. The default is used rather than the number somebody typed.

A factor written as a string is not a factor. `NaN` and the infinities are refused the same way and are not here, because JSON cannot hold one — they are in the unit suites of both editions instead, which is where a value the corpus format cannot express has to be checked.

The interesting one. §54.4 says the OS enforces a timeout and does not say what to do about a skill that declares no duration, so this reports that it cannot be enforced rather than inventing a ceiling. Refusing an unbounded skill and permitting one are both defensible, and the decision belongs where policy is made.
Milliseconds are integers. Half rounds up, which is JavaScript’s `Math.round` and is why the sign of both operands is checked before the multiplication rather than after it.
A twenty-minute skill, which is still bounded.
